question.text: A Self-Regulatory Organization (SRO) in the Indian securities market must:

answer.text: Operate independently without any SEBI oversight
Be recognized by SEBI and always abide by SEBI's directions

explanation.text: The Logic: An SRO must be recognized by SEBI and must always abide by SEBI's directions while acting in the best interest of investors. The definition explicitly excludes a stock exchange from being treated as an SRO, and SEBI also nominates directors on the SRO's board. The Trap: SROs are not stock exchanges — stock exchanges are explicitly excluded from the SRO definition in the workbook. SROs represent intermediary segments under SEBI's continuous oversight. Note: Source basis is p.93 of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook (June 2025).
